privacy.title: Data Security & Privacy
privacy.l1: Storage: core data such as transactions, accounts, and categories is stored in your local or self-hosted database by default, and is not uploaded automatically by LedgerFlow.
privacy.l2: Encrypted transport: use HTTPS for AI requests whenever possible; the API key is used only for requests to your configured provider.
privacy.l3: Minimal context: only necessary context is sent when you trigger AI features, avoiding redundant data exposure.
privacy.l4: Privacy protection: review and remove sensitive notes before export/sharing.

help.title: From recording every entry to understanding your money
help.description: Follow the order below as you use the app. Finish the step in front of you first; you can add the rest whenever you need.
help.startDescription: Record one transaction, then check that the account balance and category match your habits.

flow.title: Start with one transaction
flow.description: Record income and expenses as they actually happen. You do not need to get the category and account perfect on the first try.

steps.1: Click “Add transaction” and enter the amount, category, account, and date.
steps.2: For a large batch, import WeChat Pay or Alipay statements from Transactions.
steps.3: You can edit or delete a mistaken entry, or move it to the recycle bin.

accounts.title: Make account balances trustworthy
accounts.description: Accounts hold cash, bank cards, and payment balances; categories explain where the money went.

steps.1: Create your regular accounts and expense categories under Accounts & Categories.
steps.2: Use the transfer type for transfers so the same money is not counted as two expenses.
steps.3: If a balance looks wrong, check the latest changes in Balance Changes first.

plan.title: Plan for future expenses
plan.description: Budgets and repayments are not just after-the-fact reports. They help you see pressure early.

steps.1: Set a monthly total or category limit with Smart Budget, then adjust it as real spending comes in.
steps.2: For debt, start by recording the next repayment date, item, and amount.
steps.3: Add installments, interest rates, or a payment schedule when needed; the trend will show future repayments.

backup.title: Back up, migrate, and restore
backup.description: Your chosen database is the source of truth; backups are for migration and recovery.

steps.1: After choosing SQLite or MySQL during setup, the configuration is stored in the persistent data directory.
steps.2: Export JSON from backup settings, or configure remote backups such as WebDAV or object storage.
steps.3: Create a fresh backup before restoring; restoring overwrites data in the selected scope.

faq.title: Start here when something goes wrong
faq.databaseStatusQuestion: Why do I see “Database status check temporarily failed”?
faq.databaseStatusAnswer: When the page cannot reach the local API or database status endpoint, it keeps showing the last confirmed configuration. Make sure the service is running and the data directory is writable, then retry the check in backup settings.
faq.sqliteLocationAnswer: In a container deployment, SQLite writes to the app data directory. Mount that directory to the host or a persistent volume. If you rebuild the container without mounting the data directory, the database file may be lost with the container.
faq.aiQuestion: Why is the AI assistant not answering or unable to browse the web?
faq.aiAnswer: Check the model URL, model name, and API key in Settings. Web search also needs one provider configured under Web search (Tavily, Brave, Serper, Exa, or Google CSE). Without it, the AI can still analyze your local ledger.
faq.shortcutsQuestion: Do keyboard shortcuts fire inside input fields?
faq.shortcutsAnswer: No. Shortcuts are disabled while the cursor is in an input, text area, or editable content. Use N to add a transaction, A to open the assistant, B to open Smart Budget, G to go home, H to open Help, D to open backup settings, and / to search transactions.
